ardms-spi-readiness-check-artifacts-safe.prompt: Which condition makes the thermal index for bone (TIB) the most relevant displayed thermal index?

options.text: The beam traverses only homogeneous soft tissue with no bone near the focus
A color variance map shows a broad velocity distribution
A matching layer is being checked during probe manufacture
Ossified bone at or near the focus, where heating concentrates

ardms-spi-readiness-check-artifacts-safe.explanation: TIB estimates temperature rise when bone is at or near the beam focus. Bone absorbs ultrasound strongly, so this model is more relevant than the soft-tissue index when the focal region includes ossified bone.

distractorExplanations.a: Homogeneous soft tissue without bone near the focus is modeled by a soft-tissue thermal index rather than TIB.
distractorExplanations.b: Color variance describes velocity spread and is not an acoustic-heating safety index.
distractorExplanations.c: Matching-layer inspection is a manufacturing task and does not determine which patient thermal index applies.

options.text: Use receiver gain before increasing acoustic output
Keep output at 100% and reduce gain as the first step
Hide MI and TI readouts so they cannot influence scanning
Hold high output indefinitely while the image is frozen
The on-screen MI value without any independent acoustic measurement
A calibrated hydrophone plus radiation-force power measurements
A grayscale tissue phantom with calipers but no pressure sensor
A Doppler flow phantom used only to verify displayed velocity

distractorExplanations.a: MI is a derived operator index; regulatory characterization relies on calibrated measurements of the acoustic field.
distractorExplanations.c: A grayscale phantom checks imaging performance, not absolute acoustic pressure or output power.
distractorExplanations.d: A flow phantom checks Doppler measurement performance and cannot replace calibrated acoustic-output instrumentation.

ardms-spi-readiness-check-doppler-hemody.prompt: A spectral waveform appears below the baseline after the probe orientation and steering are changed. Before reporting a true flow-direction change, what should the operator verify?

options.text: Raise the wall filter until the directional waveform is removed
Enable tissue harmonics to reverse the spectral frequency shift
Increase ensemble length so the spectral baseline flips automatically
Check spectral invert, beam steering, angle geometry, and a known reference direction

ardms-spi-readiness-check-doppler-hemody.explanation: Spectral polarity depends on motion relative to the beam and on display inversion. Verifying invert, steering, angle geometry, and a known reference direction separates a setup change from a genuine reversal without making a clinical diagnosis from display polarity alone.

distractorExplanations.a: The wall filter suppresses low-frequency shifts; erasing the waveform cannot validate its direction.
distractorExplanations.b: Tissue harmonics affect B-mode image formation and do not reverse spectral Doppler polarity.
distractorExplanations.c: Ensemble length affects estimate stability and temporal resolution, not spectral baseline polarity.

options.text: Velocity aliasing from sampling a shift above the Nyquist limit

distractorExplanations.a: Velocity aliasing wraps frequencies across the baseline; it does not assign late echoes to the wrong depth.
distractorExplanations.b: Mirror image duplicates anatomy across a strong reflector rather than misassigning a late pulse echo in range.
distractorExplanations.d: Spectral broadening widens the velocity distribution and is not a pulse-to-pulse depth assignment error.

ardms-spi-readiness-check-transducers-be.prompt: During transducer manufacture, a PZT element is accidentally heated above its Curie temperature. What is the likely result?

options.text: Its center frequency rises temporarily, but polarization is unchanged
Its polarization is lost, destroying normal piezoelectric behavior
Its matching layer automatically changes from quarter-wave to half-wave thickness
It becomes a continuous-wave element while retaining receive sensitivity

ardms-spi-readiness-check-transducers-be.explanation: Heating polarized PZT above its Curie temperature can depolarize the ceramic, so it no longer converts electrical and mechanical energy normally. Routine probe care must follow the manufacturer’s temperature and disinfection limits, but an autoclave does not necessarily exceed the Curie point.

distractorExplanations.a: Crossing the Curie temperature can permanently depolarize PZT; it is not merely a reversible frequency shift.
distractorExplanations.c: Matching-layer thickness is a physical construction dimension and does not double when the crystal is overheated.
distractorExplanations.d: Continuous-wave operation depends on transducer construction and excitation, not Curie-temperature damage.
